discontinuity.def: A point where a function is not continuous: its graph breaks there. At $x = c$ this happens when $f(c)$ is undefined, when $\lim_{x \to c} f(x)$ does not exist, or when the two are not equal.

removable-discontinuity.def: A discontinuity at $x = c$ where $\lim_{x \to c} f(x)$ exists, but $f(c)$ is undefined or not equal to it. The graph has a hole, possibly with a dot elsewhere above or below it.

jump-discontinuity.def: A discontinuity at $x = c$ where both one-sided limits exist as finite numbers but are not equal, so the graph jumps from one height to another.

infinite-discontinuity.def: A discontinuity at $x = c$ where the function is unbounded on at least one side of $c$. The graph has a vertical asymptote $x = c$.
